To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the majority of firms in the peripherial sector exhibit income smoothing, while a minority of firms in the core exhibit income smoothing, and (2) the peripherial firms are more likely to exhibit income smoothing.

(1) there are systematic differences in the smoothing of income numbers between the core and the periphery industrial sectors; and (2) these differences are related to the different opportunity structure and experiences of the firms in the two sectors.

the effects of the duality of the economy on income smoothing practices.
the effects of the duality of the Nigerian economy on the behavior of firms in the two sectors.
the effects of the duality of the Nigerian industrial sector on the income numbers smoothing behavior of firms.

the smoothing of income numbers is not a phenomenon that is confined to the periphery sector, but that the smoothing is more prevalent among firms in the peripheral sector.
income smoothing is a common and pervasive phenomenon in both the core and periphery sectors.
the smoothing behavior of firms in the peripheries is more extensive than that of firms in the cores.

the smoothing of income numbers is a more widespread phenomenon among firms in the dual economy.
